title: Test PowerShell witness commands under-escape an apostrophe in the temp path across nested single-quote layers
outcome:
src/tests/test_child_temp.rs (the grandchild TEMP witness, :56/:60) escapes the marker path once (' -> '') but embeds it in two nested PowerShell single-quoted layers: the parent's -ArgumentList element and the grandchild's WriteAllText argument. A test temp path with an apostrophe (e.g. C:\Users\O'Neil\…) would make the grandchild command malformed and fail the witness at its marker read, even though TEMP containment is correct. The same pattern is pre-existing at src/tests/terminal.rs:1825 and :1841 (terminal_timeout_process_tree_command and terminal_background_process_tree_command). Fix: pass the marker to the grandchild through an inherited environment variable, or escape each quoting layer independently, with a shared helper for all three call sites.

A related optional follow-up, a reviewer Note: give the two root-as-workdir process-tree tests in src/tests/terminal.rs (timeout_kills_process_tree and cleans_up_background_children_after_shell_exit) a TestTempRoot guard. A panic before their trailing remove_dir_all would otherwise leave a root now holding the killed grandchild's probe residue in child-temp.
acceptance: Test PowerShell witness commands under-escape an apostrophe in the temp path across nested single-quote layers is done
